extracted.intended_audience: English learners and writers seeking guidance on correct usage of the word "the"
extracted.subtask_description: Explain and identify when the word 'the' functions as a definite article versus when it functions as an adverb, with usage rules and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part of speech classification for 'the'
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'the' can be one of two parts of speech, depending on how it’s used: a definite article (when it comes before a noun) or an adverb (when it modifies a verb, an adjective, or a group of words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contextual tests: if 'the' appears before a noun and refers to something specific or creates a proper noun, treat it as the definite article; if it modifies a verb, adjective, another adverb, or a phrase, treat it as an adverb. (From text: "The can be one of two parts of speech... When it comes before a noun... it’s a definite article. The can also be used as an adverb to modify a verb, an adjective, or a group of words.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Definite-article usage (referencing specific/known entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The' as a definite article refers to a specific person, place, or thing known or implied to be known by the reader or listener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'the' when referring to something that’s known to your audience or has been previously discussed. Example: "My neighbor caught the dog in their yard this morning." Contrast with the indefinite article: "My neighbor found a dog..." which is unspecific. The article often implies prior discussion or shared knowledge. The page also notes 'the' may be used to create a proper noun (e.g., names like 'the Hague').

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural-noun and omission guidance for articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles (including 'the') are used with nouns; with plural nouns you can use a definite article or omit the article altogether.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states: "As a reminder, use definite articles with plural nouns; you can also omit the article with plural nouns." Guidance: choose 'the' when referring to a specific set/groups known to listener; omit when speaking of plural nouns in general (e.g., 'Cats are independent' vs 'The cats in my house are independent').

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles as determiners (grammatical classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are a part of speech used to identify nouns and are also known as determiners; determiners are considered a type of adjective because they describe the nouns they precede.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding that articles function as determiners helps explain their role in noun phrases and agreement/placement rules. (From text: "Articles are also known as determiners, which are considered a type of adjective because they describe the nouns they’re placed in front of.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverbial senses of 'the' (three definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When used as an adverb, 'the' has three definitions: (1) 'than before' or 'than otherwise'; (2) 'to what extent' or 'to that extent'; and (3) 'beyond all others.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples supplied: 1) 'Switch your seat—the teacher will be none the wiser.' (sense: than before/than otherwise); 2) 'The sooner the better.' (sense: to what extent/to that extent); 3) 'Rosa’s is the best pizza place in New York City.' (sense: beyond all others). Note that adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, other adverbs, or groups of words; 'the' as an adverb commonly appears in comparative contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative and correlative constructions using 'the'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The' is often used in comparisons and in correlative comparative constructions (the X, the Y), and it can modify adjectives to compare one item to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage examples: 'We thought Michaelangelo had the best painting in the class.' (modifies 'best' to compare one painting to the others); 'The hotter the better.' and 'The sooner the better.' illustrate the correlative comparative pattern where 'the' appears twice to link two comparative clauses. Use this pattern to express proportional or correlative relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverbial-phrase formation with 'the'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The' can form part of adverbial phrases (a group of words acting as an adverb) to indicate degree, probability, or extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'It’s looking all the more likely we’ll be staying home for Christmas.' The phrase 'all the more likely' functions as an adverbial phrase expressing increased probability. When encountering multiword phrases beginning with 'the', test whether the phrase as a whole modifies a verb/adjective/adverb to classify it as adverbial usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing usage from examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete sentence examples help identify whether 'the' functions as an article or an adverb in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides multiple examples (e.g., 'That’s the king of England.' 'He’s the dog of my dreams.' 'The hotter the better.' 'The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal.' 'That’s the spirit!') — read examples to see the role 'the' plays: directly before a noun (article) vs before an adjective/comparative or within idiomatic phrases (adverb). Use such examples as diagnostic patterns when classifying 'the' in new sentences.
